issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: The template declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)), while the problem statement's task description and UML (problem_statement.md) specify addGuestStudents(int) and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). This mismatch between the template and the problem/solution files will confuse students about which signature to implement and can cause compilation errors if they follow one artifact but not the other.

The exercise requires a method to add guest students. The problem statement and the solution use the identifier and signature addGuestStudents(int) (problem statement: "addGuestStudents(int)"; solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents)). However, the template defines a different signature: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This introduces a naming/parameter mismatch for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) and will confuse students: they cannot directly map the required method from the description to the template stub, and unit tests or the provided solution expecting a single-parameter method will not match the two-parameter stub.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by removing the extra boolean parameter. Change the template stub to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement */ } so students see and implement the expected single-parameter method.
